newsitem.title: USA: U.S. charges militia suspects in Calif. bomb case.
newsitem.headline: U.S. charges militia suspects in Calif. bomb case.

text.p: Federal prosecutors filed charges on Friday against two men suspected of links to anti-government groups for possessing 550 pounds of explosives allegedly stolen from an underground bunker in Wyoming.

The men -- Kevin Quinn, 37, and Vernon Weckner, 66 -- were each charged with two felony counts of possessing the stolen petrogel explosives and two cases of electric detonators, federal prosecutors said.
Law enforcement officers said they recovered the petrogel and blasting caps from Weckner's motor home in Yuba City, 50 miles (80 kms) north of Sacramento, on April 30.

Authorities said the explosives were stolen from oil and gas exploration firm Reliable Exploration Inc. Quinn worked for one its sub-contractors in Gillette, Wyoming, according to an affidavit filed in U.S. District Court in Sacramento.

One of Quinn's co-workers in Wyoming, Allan Carpenter, told investigators how he and Quinn stole the explosives and blasting caps from Reliable Exploration and drove them to Yuba City, where they tried to sell them to Weckner and others.
A total of 10 suspects are currently in custody in the explosives case. Officials said the explosives "could have leveled three city blocks" had they gone off.
Yuba County Undersheriff Gary Finch said some of those arrested were "hard-core militia types."
"I have no idea what they were going to do," Finch said. "The folks are unhappy about something. They advocate threats against government officials."
Weckner is the elder figure of a local band of constitutionalists known as the Twin Cities Free Militia, the Sacramento Bee reported.

They were arrested after an explosion last month at the house of William Goehler, who supported the anti-government Freemen group in Montana last year. The blast, which could be heard for miles, caused extensive damage to the home and broke windows in nearby buildings.

Goehler suffered a neck injury while his wife Debbie and one of his children were slightly injured. Authorities believe explosives stored in a tree near the house blew up. Goehler faces state charges for involvement in the case, Finch said.
Local news reports said Goehler went to Montana during last year's Freemen standoff, spending weeks near the militants' compound carrying an upside-down American flag.

The heavily armed Freemen, who rejected U.S. government authority, set up what they saw as an independent state on a Montana ranch, calling it "Justus Township." They eventually surrendered to authorities.
